Ana — quick technical note from infra side. We can support a month‑start exception window with two approaches:

Option A — Elevated latency threshold: define a higher per‑request latency threshold for the 1st 6 hours (e.g., p95 target 400ms instead of 200ms). Credits are calculated against the active threshold.
Option B — Window-exclusion: exclude the 6‑hour window from monthly uptime calculations entirely; uptime is computed on the remainder of the month.

Operational tradeoffs: Option A keeps SLAs meaningful during the window and aligns with existing multi-tenant scheduling; Option B is simpler for billing but incentives could be misaligned for sustained outages outside the window.

Suggested language (short):
"During the agreed monthly maintenance window (the first six hours beginning at 00:00 UTC on the first day of each calendar month), the Service Availability and latency targets in this Order Form will be measured against an elevated latency threshold. Credits for incidents occurring during this window will be calculated against the elevated threshold and not the standard production threshold."

If CardioCloud prefers exclusion from monthly uptime, we can draft that variant too.

—Marcus

Ana / Vanessa — attaching a redline for the MSA/SOW and an order form addendum. Notes in summary:

- We propose the "elevated latency threshold" approach (Option A) with a clear definition of the measurement window (00:00–06:00 UTC on the first day of the month).
- Credit formula: prorated minutes below threshold, capped per month at 10% of the monthly invoice. Language included in the attached msasow_redlines_cardio.docx.
- We include a fallback clause: if the elevated threshold is exceeded for more than two calendar days in a row (outside the agreed window), Redwood will engage remediation cadence and credits will revert to the standard formula for the impacted period.

Please see attached redline (msasow_redlines_cardio.docx) and an inline order form clause pasted below for quick review. If that looks acceptable, Vanessa — can you confirm commercial approval for the 10% cap and we’ll produce final addendum for signature?

Inline suggested order form addendum (snippet):
"Service Availability — Month‑Start Window: During the first six hours beginning at 00:00 UTC on the first day of each calendar month, the parties agree that the Service will be measured using an elevated latency threshold of 400ms P95. Credits for incidents occurring during this window shall be calculated against the elevated threshold. Credits are capped at 10% of the applicable monthly subscription fee. Repeated elevated‑threshold breaches beyond two consecutive days will trigger an escalation and revert to standard credit calculations for the impacted timeframe."
